clue.text: Better set up cover for organ control

parts.note: to better is to beat or outdo, which is to trump

indicators.note: up here means in disorder, as in things being all up, so the word set is jumbled

parts.note: a top is a lid or cover

explanation.surface: Someone praises an improved casing for part of a church organ's workings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is a verb here (to outdo), not a comparative; 'up' signals that the following word is jumbled into ETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumpet stop is an organ stop: a knob that brings in a reed rank imitating that brass instrument.

clue.text: Porter carries tons — a big lie?

indicators.note: the porter is carrying the T, here placed at the front of the word for the porter

parts.note: one who humps (lugs) loads about is a humper

explanation.surface: A question whether a porter claiming to carry tons is telling a whopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumper is informal for something huge of its kind, especially a whopping falsehood.

clue.text: The act of going into a ruin is misinterpreted

indicators.note: letters that are misinterpreted are read in a wrong order, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone protests that going into a ruined building has been misread as something else.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Going' is a coy euphemism for passing water, and this is the formal word for that act.

clue.text: Longing to see province take part in online test

indicators.note: the province takes part in the test by entering the middle of it

parts.note: a ping is a network test sent to see whether a computer answers
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called the Province

explanation.surface: Someone keen to see a region join in an internet quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: Pining is yearning or longing for something absent, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Allegro maybe encountered travelling north over river

indicators.note: in a down answer, the first piece sits over the second
in a down clue, travelling north means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: to have encountered is to have met
the Po is the great river of northern Italy

explanation.surface: A brisk musical passage apparently met while heading north across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'travelling north' suits a down light, where reading upwards means reading backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical speed marking, an example of a tempo, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Signal originally heard after English side's caught in ambush

indicators.note: the letter from 'heard' comes after the rest
the English side is caught inside the ambush, sitting within its letters

parts.note: a trap is an ambush
leg is a side of a cricket field (the 's is 'is')

indicators.note: the original letter of heard is its first one

explanation.surface: A warning heard after an English team is caught in an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: The leg side is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs; the 's of 'side's' is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: To telegraph is to signal: make plain in advance, as a boxer telegraphs a punch.

clue.text: Doctor's removing top in virgin's treatment

indicators.note: the shortened doctor goes inside the word for virgin

parts.note: pure, as in virgin snow, unsullied

indicators.note: removing the top of the word means dropping its first letter

parts.note: a medic is a doctor (the 's is 'is')

explanation.surface: A doctor carrying out a procedure on a virgin's body.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Doctor's' is 'is'; 'removing top' beheads the doctor and 'in' places the remainder inside the word for virgin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicure is a cosmetic treatment of the feet and toenails.

clue.text: Miss France leaves upset

indicators.note: France leaves the word, so its letter is dropped

parts.note: to miss a target is to fail
F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A beauty queen, Miss France, walks out in a huff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss France' reads as a pageant title; it is two pieces, and 'upset' is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to trouble or afflict, so 'what ails you' means what is upsetting you.

clue.text: Conscious of reverence surrounding a king

indicators.note: the word for reverence wraps round the other letters

parts.note: awe is deep reverence
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone aware of the deference shown around a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being awake, as in 'awake to the danger', means being alert and aware of it.

clue.text: Springtime opened up opportunity for women?

definitions.meaning: read as a time to spring: a jump day
by tradition, 29 February is the one day a woman may propose marriage

explanation.definitionFit: The 29th of February, every fourth year, is the traditional day for women to propose, and literally a day for leaping.

clue.text: Peacekeepers' boss returning for wedding

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: returning means the word for boss is read backwards

parts.note: the boss is number one, written NO 1, NO I

explanation.surface: The head of the peacekeeping force comes back home for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns NO I (number one) into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together, and a marriage is the union of two people.

clue.text: It may feature emotional role with madam

definitions.text: It may feature emotional role with madam

indicators.note: an emotional state is agitated, so these letters are worked up into a new order

explanation.surface: A description of a stage genre in which an actress plays a tearful madam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'emotional' shuffles ROLE and MADAM together; the whole clue also describes the genre.
explanation.definitionFit: Overwrought stage drama full of heightened feeling is the classic setting for a highly emotional role.

clue.text: Frank's playing German church music

parts.note: frank means plain-spoken, plain; with the 's it gives the plural-looking form
something playing, as a film, is on

explanation.surface: A man called Frank is playing German sacred music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name; it means plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Plainsong is unaccompanied medieval chant used in church liturgy, such as Gregorian chant.

clue.text: Principles of mediocre editor

indicators.note: the answer is made of letters taken from inside the next two words

explanation.surface: A complaint about the beliefs of a second-rate editor.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a set of beliefs or guiding principles, as in a religious statement of faith.

clue.text: Gunners' stylish volley

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the Gunners
in, as in fashionable or in vogue

explanation.surface: Artillerymen fire an elegant volley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volley' sounds military but means a shower, as in a rain of blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain of arrows or blows is a heavy shower of them, just as a volley is.

clue.text: Woman from posh part of London ignores first American musical

indicators.note: the woman comes from the district, so its name is placed in front
the earlier of the two matching letters in the district's name is left out

parts.note: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London
a lady is a woman

explanation.surface: A lady from a smart London district snubs the first American she meets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores first' drops the first A of MAYFAIR, leaving MYFAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lerner and Loewe stage show based on Shaw's Pygmalion is a famous musical.

clue.text: Time with Heather's racehorses

parts.note: a year is a period of time
ling is common heather; with the 's it becomes lings

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather spends time with her racehorses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a name; it is the plant ling.
explanation.definitionFit: Young racehorses in their second calendar year, between one and two, are known by this term.

clue.text: Lancaster's illegitimate according to inheritance

indicators.note: an illegitimate form is not the proper one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A claim that the House of Lancaster's heir is illegitimate in the line of succession.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the letters of 'Lancaster' are rearranged; the 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancestral is handed down from forebears, so it comes by inheritance.

clue.text: Anxious Australian soldier thanks Edward

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
ta is informal British for thanks
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A nervous Australian soldier thanks a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitated means nervously disturbed or worried, close in sense to anxious.

clue.text: Specialist books: Rebuilding Phonograms

indicators.note: rebuilding a word means putting its letters together in a new order

explanation.surface: A title for specialist volumes on restoring old gramophones.
explanation.definitionFit: A monograph is a scholarly book on one specialised subject.

clue.text: Print Starbucks' warning?

definitions.meaning: a police photograph of a suspect taken on arrest, like a fingerprint record
a coffee chain might warn that the cup is scalding

explanation.definitionFit: A police photograph of an arrested person's face is a print of it, and split up the word warns that a coffee cup is scalding.

clue.text: Some computers returned in dodgy scheme

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Macs are Apple computers, some of all computers

explanation.surface: Some returned computers turn out to be part of a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent or dishonest scheme, a con.

clue.text: Man going round Northern church

indicators.note: the word for a man goes round the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: mister is a form of address for a man

explanation.surface: A man walking around a church in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: A minster is a large or important church, such as York Minster.

clue.text: Briefly sleep with first lady in African capital!

indicators.note: said briefly, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: kip is British slang for a sleep
gal is a girl or lady
first is number one, written as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a quick nap with a leading woman in an African city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' reads as a president's wife; it is two pieces, GAL then I.
explanation.definitionFit: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda in central Africa.

clue.text: Clear about the Italian's culpability

indicators.note: the word for clear goes about the Italian article, enclosing it

parts.note: to gut a building is to clear out its interior
il is 'the' in Italian (the 's is 'is')

explanation.surface: Someone cleared over an Italian's wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the fact of having done wrong, which is what culpability means.

clue.text: Hint's easily uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered means its top is taken off, so the first letter goes

parts.note: simply means easily, without difficulty

explanation.surface: A hint that is easily seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Hint's' is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest without stating outright, much as to hint does.

clue.text: Cohabit, as it happens, in Southern Indiana

parts.note: a live broadcast goes out as it happens
IN is the postal code for Indiana

explanation.surface: A couple living together, as chance has it, in the south of Indiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as it happens' looks like a filler phrase; it means live.
explanation.definitionFit: Living in sin is the old-fashioned phrase for an unmarried couple sharing a home.

clue.text: In Germany I may invade abandoned varsity town in France

indicators.note: the German pronoun invades the emptied word, going into it
abandoned means left empty, so only the outer letters of varsity remain

parts.note: ich is the German for I

explanation.surface: A German may invade a deserted university town in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' means emptied, keeping only the ends of 'varsity'; 'invade' puts the German word for I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Vichy is a spa town in central France, seat of the wartime collaborationist government.

clue.text: Tiny pooch suffering, lacking muscle tone

indicators.note: something suffering is in a bad way, so the letters are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A little dog that is ill and has gone floppy.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine hypotonic describes muscles with abnormally low tension, so it means lacking tone.

clue.text: Legendary creature attending around end of the working week

indicators.note: the word for attending goes around the day, enclosing it

parts.note: being at an event is attending it
Fri, Friday, ends the working week

explanation.surface: A mythical beast turns up at around Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful demon or jinn of Arabic mythology.

clue.text: Closed with unknown play

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A shut room holding a mysterious play.
explanation.definitionFit: To toy with something is to play with it idly.

clue.text: Originally study factory owner's plant

indicators.note: the word study is not in its original order, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: a miller owns a mill, a factory

explanation.surface: A first study of a mill owner's factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like the factory; it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusty miller is the name of several silvery-leaved garden plants, such as a cineraria.
